title: lambdag-lab: multilingual grammar-based authorship verification
description:
Multilingual, grammar-based authorship verification for literary and historical texts: POSNoise topic masking in 23 languages, including Middle High and Middle Low German, a single-file, Numba-accelerated implementation of the LambdaG method with three interchangeable probability engines (Kneser-Ney, Hierarchical Pitman-Yor, PPMd), forensic calibration reporting likelihood ratios and the log-likelihood-ratio cost with its decomposition, and token-level explainability heat maps.

This release accompanies Łukasz Gągała, "Grammar on Trial: Forensic Authorship Verification across Twenty-Three Languages and Three Genres", Proceedings of the Computational Humanities Research Conference 2027. Its reproduction kit is in papers/2027-chr/, whose README maps each table and figure to the script that produced it. The 19 treebank-mined POSNoise pattern lists the paper releases are in posnoise_lists/, with the tools that built and validated them. papers/2027-chr/data/ holds the per-case score files behind every number the paper reports, with a standalone script that recomputes its headline median AUC from them, so a reported figure can be checked without rebuilding the corpora or rerunning the grid.

This is an independent research implementation and extension suite. For the reference implementation of the LambdaG method by its author, see AndreaNini/LambdaG; the R implementation is idiolect. The method is due to Nini et al., the POSNoise masking approach to Halvani and Graner (2021).

The code is released under the Apache-2.0 licence. The per-case score files are released under CC0-1.0: they hold aggregate statistics per case and no token, text, title or author name, so they carry no licence obligation from the corpora the cases were built on.
